SK9028 An input the gate's scoping depends on could not be read

An input the gate's scoping depends on could not be read: --since=<ref> did not resolve, the baseline the gate names does not exist, the baseline exists but will not parse, or --no-new-suppressions could not compare against its reference. The gate does not fail on this id itself — but its inputs change: a missing or unreadable baseline counts every finding as new, and an unresolvable --since leaves findings unscoped, so a newIssues gate then fails with 0 accepted, N new and this line is the only explanation.

Since2.0

Why

These four were reported as SK9030 "an analyzer threw", which none of them is. Sharing the id meant SK9030 could not be read as "a rule died" — the one question #295 wanted answered — and the gate could not be made to fail on a crash without also failing on a missing baseline file. Failing in the safe direction is deliberate: an absent baseline makes every finding new rather than every finding accepted. skala baseline create --apply writes one; a shallow CI clone is the usual reason a --since ref does not resolve.

When it does not fire

Only a baseline the gate definition or --baseline names is reported when absent; the default path is used only if it exists, so a repository that has never baselined sees no diagnostic and its findings are bucketed as unknown rather than new. The missing-baseline form is a warning where the other three are errors, so the GitHub log shows it as ::notice:: and the others as ::error::; none of the four is a gate failure in itself.
